statements.t: Commercially, we advanced key customer projects, including our 280 MW Arcadia eFuels agreement and broader partnership covering more than 1 GW of potential projects.

The Company’s EBITDAS-positive target for Q4 2026 is a forward-looking non-GAAP financial measure that cannot be reconciled to the most directly comparable GAAP measure, net income (loss), without unreasonable efforts.

This is because the Company is not able to forecast with reasonable accuracy certain items required for such reconciliation, including interest expense associated with financial arrangements, income taxes, and other non-cash or infrequent charges.
The Company provides this target to give investors insight into the direction of its operational objectives rather than as a prediction of GAAP earnings.

statements.t: The decrease was primarily due to headcount reductions resulting from the Company’s 2025 Restructuring Plan as well as a decrease in government-sponsored research and development project expense, partially offset by an increase in system and component materials expense.

The future use of our available liquidity will be based upon the ongoing review of the funding needs of our businesses, the optimal allocation of our resources, and the timing of cash flow generation.
Key assumptions are based on factors such as forecasted sales and costs, the Company’s right to direct B.

During the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026, the Company recorded impairment charges of $15.6 million and $20.8 million, respectively, related to the Company’s property, plant and equipment, net primarily due to assets that are no longer in service and projects that are no longer probable of being completed.

On February 24, 2026, our joint venture, AccionaPlug S.L., entered into a subsidy agreement with the European Hydrogen Bank, which is managed by Instituto para la Diversificación y Ahorro de la Energía (“IDAE”), a Spanish governing body, to subsidize a renewable hydrogen production project in Spain.
The Company has provided a guarantee of €7.5 million which can be called by IDAE if the joint venture fails to meet its performance targets under the subsidy agreement.
